title: Mixtures and Separation Techniques
seo_title: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Mixtures and Separation Techniques Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Mixtures are combinations of substances that can be separated by physical methods such as picking, sieving, filtering, decanting, evaporation, magnetic separation and distillation. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): pure substances and mixtures, kinds of mixtures, separating mixtures, separation methods and separation in industry and the environment. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
body_html:
How to think about it

A pure substance has only one kind of particle; a mixture has two or more. In a heterogeneous mixture you can see the different parts, like gravel and sand or oil and water.

Mixtures are separated by differences in their parts: sieving and filtering use particle size, settling and flotation use density, and a magnet pulls out iron. Mines use these methods to separate valuable minerals from rock.

Example

How can you separate sand from water?

Sand particles are bigger than the holes in paper.

Answer: filter it

Example

Oil floats on water. Which property separates them?

Which one is less dense?

Answer: density

Common mistakes

  • Thinking you can filter out dissolved salt.
  • Calling salt water a heterogeneous mixture (it is a solution).
  • Forgetting that a magnet only picks up iron, nickel and cobalt.

items.q: What is the principle behind magnetic attraction?
c: Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
items.e: This is how magnetic attraction works.

sets.title: Separation in industry and the environment

items.q: What is the best way to separate wood chips and sand?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Wood floats in water and sand sinks, so the wood chips can be skimmed off.

items.q: In a chromatogram, a food colouring gives two spots. What does this show?
c: It is a mixture of two dyes.
items.e: A pure dye gives only one spot.

items.q: What is the best way to separate oil and water?
c: add water and skim off what floats
let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: Oil does not dissolve in water; it floats as a layer on top that can be poured or scooped off.

items.q: What does soluble mean?
c: able to dissolve in a solvent
items.e: Salt is soluble in water.

items.q: What is the best way to separate sand and water?
c: add water and skim off what floats
let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: The filter paper lets water through but stops the sand grains.

items.q: How can you get pure dry salt from a mixture of salt and sand?
c: Add water and stir, filter, then evaporate the filtrate.
items.e: Salt dissolves; sand does not.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of pebbles and sand?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
add water and skim off what floats
items.e: The small sand grains fall through the holes in the screen, and the pebbles stay on top.

items.q: Which method separates the inks in a marker?
items.e: Each ink travels up the paper at a different speed.

items.q: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. A mixture of the two is heated. Which liquid is collected first?
items.e: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils off first.

items.q: What is a solute?
c: the substance that does the dissolving
a solid that does not dissolve
items.e: Sugar is the solute in sugar water.

items.q: What is distillation?
c: boiling a liquid and condensing the vapour to collect a pure liquid
items.e: Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points.

items.q: Why does a sieve separate gravel from sand?
c: The holes let small sand grains through but stop larger gravel.
items.e: Sieving uses particle size.

items.q: Which method gets salt back from salt water?
items.e: The water evaporates and leaves the salt.

items.q: Bisi dissolves 8 g of salt in 100 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Dayo mixes 5 g of sand with 50 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: What is a saturated solution?
c: a mixture of sand and water
a solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature
items.e: Extra solute sinks to the bottom.

items.q: Which method separates pebbles and sand?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: The small sand grains fall through the holes in the screen, and the pebbles stay on top.

items.q: Abdullahi mixes 20 g of sand with 150 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Abdullahi dissolves 10 g of salt in 100 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: What is concentration?
c: the amount of solute in a certain amount of solution
items.e: More solute means higher concentration.
